title: Scalable Power Sampling: Unlocking Efficient, Training-Free Reasoning for LLMs via Distribution Sharpening
abstract: arXiv:2601.21590v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training is a dominant approach for improving the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), yet growing evidence suggests that its gains arise primarily from distribution sharpening rather than the acquisition of new capabilities. Recent work has shown that sampling from the power distribution of LLMs using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) can recover performance comparable to RL post-training without relying on external rewards; however, the high computational cost of MCMC makes such approaches impractical for widespread adoption. In this work, we propose a theoretically grounded alternative that eliminates the need for iterative MCMC. We derive a token-level decomposition of the autoregressive power distribution, showing that the global power distribution can be approximated by a token-level scaled low-temperature one, where the scaling factor captures future trajectory quality. translated_title: 可扩展的幂采样：通过分布锐化解锁大语言模型的高效免训练推理
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）后训练是提升大语言模型（LLM）推理性能的主流方法，然而越来越多的证据表明，其收益主要来源于分布锐化而非新能力的获取。近期研究表明，利用马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛（MCMC）从LLM的幂分布中采样，可以在不依赖外部奖励的情况下获得与RL后训练相当的性能；然而，MCMC高昂的计算成本使这类方法难以被广泛采用。在本工作中，我们提出了一种有理论基础、无需迭代MCMC的替代方案。我们推导了自回归幂分布的token级分解，证明全局幂分布可以通过token级缩放的低温分布来近似，其中缩放因子刻画了未来轨迹的质量。
tldr: 本文提出一种可扩展的幂采样方法，通过将自回归幂分布分解为token级缩放的低温分布来近似全局幂分布，从而免去迭代MCMC的高昂计算成本，以高效、免训练的方式实现与RL后训练相当的推理性能提升。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a scalable power sampling method that approximates the global power distribution through a token-level scaled low-temperature decomposition, eliminating the need for costly iterative MCMC and achieving training-free reasoning performance comparable to RL post-training.
